keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Infobox "c. 6,100-5,100 BC"; the culture "lasted between about 6100 BC and 5100 BC"; Domuztepe "occupied at least as early as c.6,200BC", its sequence starting "at the transition between the Ceramic Neolithic and the Early Halaf (c.6100 BC)". The Tigris piedmont is left to the Hassuna dossier until 5350 BCE. "Halaf-influenced material is found throughout Greater Mesopotamia" is influence, not drawn. No area figure to compare.

ledger.note: 6000 BCE: the painted-pottery villages of the Halaf hold the dry-farming belt of Upper Mesopotamia. The culture "lasted between about 6100 BC and 5100 BC" (it began a century before the project's first year); Domuztepe "was certainly founded by the Ceramic Neolithic (c.6400BC)".

region.text: Domuztepe south of Kahramanmaras, "Covering 20 hectares... the largest known settlement of that date"

ledger.note: 5450 BCE: Domuztepe, the largest Halaf settlement, is abandoned. "occupied at least as early as c.6,200BC and abandoned c.5,450BC"; "Prehistoric occupation ended towards the end of the Halaf period (c.5450 BC)".
5400 BCE: the late Halaf begins. "the Halaf-Ubaid Transitional period, which comprised the late Halaf (c. 5400-5000 BC)".

region.text: the Tigris piedmont: Tell Arpachiyah near Mosul, Nineveh, Tepe Gawra

ledger.note: 5350 BCE: the Halaf reaches the Tigris piedmont as the Hassuna villages end. Tell Arpachiyah "near Mosul", Nineveh and Tepe Gawra are Halaf sites on the page, which does not date their Halaf levels; the year is the end of the Hassuna layers at Tell Hassuna (5600-5350 BCE, Tell Hassuna page).

region.text: Upper Mesopotamia from the Euphrates bend to the Tigris

ledger.note: 5100 BCE: the Halaf becomes the northern Ubaid. "Halaf culture ended by 5000 BC after entering the so-called Halaf-Ubaid Transitional period"; "Many Halafian settlements were abandoned, and the remaining ones showed Ubaidian characters"; the page favours "a Halafian adoption of the Ubaid culture" since "there is no hiatus between the Halaf and northern Ubaid". Infobox end c. 5100 BC is used.

certainty.note: An archaeological culture: radii around excavated villages, never a frontier.

notes: Culture dossier. The Halaf began c. 6100 BC; the dossier starts at the project floor of 6000 BCE. Overlaps: the Hassuna (to 5350 BCE) holds the Tigris piedmont first; the northern Ubaid (from 5300 BCE on its own page) overlaps the late Halaf to 5100 BCE, the Halaf-Ubaid Transitional period. Early and middle Halaf are undated on the page. Gazetteer: Tell Halaf, Tell Arpachiyah, Tell Sabi Abyad, Domuztepe, Chagar Bazar, Carchemish are not places; radii around Al Hasakah, Ar Raqqah, Mardin, Gaziantep, Aleppo, Kahramanmaras and Mosul stand in. Halaf pottery "at many sites in Anatolia" and in north-west Iran is not drawn.
